Principle 19: Korean Culture
An Introduction to Korean Culture
Each and every culture is unique and special in its own way.
Korean culture is different from other culture, too.
Korean culture is not like any other culture in the world.
It has many unique aspects including its clothing, housing, names, and language.
Traditional Korean Clothing: Hanbok
First of all, Korea has its own traditional clothing known as hanbok.
In ancient times, the different styles of hanbok determined your position in society such as which social class you belonged to and whether or not you were married.
Nowadays, Koreans wear Western style clothing for every day fashion.
On traditional holidays, families celebrate by wearing the traditional hanbok.
Traditional Korean Foods: Kimchi and Bulgogi
Another unique aspect of Korean culture is its food.
Traditional Korean meals usually include boiled rice, soup, fish or meat, several vegetable side dishes, and one or more kinds of kimchi.
My favorite food is bulgogi.
Bulgogi is the most popular Korean meat dish, while the most popular vegetable dish is kimchi.
I like them both.
Traditional Korean Language: Hangul
Finally, the Korean language is not like any other world language.
Up until the middle of the 15th century, Korea didn't have its own alphabet.
Instead, they Chinese characters were used in order to write.
Most people couldn't read or write.
The only people who could read were the scholars or the nobility.
However, in 1420, the current King at that time, Se-jong, asked his royal scholars to create a unique Korean alphabet.
Soon a writing system known as hangul was created.
